title: Table

ports.note: Every port a table can show, on every table, whatever its parameters say. The ports used to vary with an inputMode parameter -- reasoningInput, polygonInput and a table mode were three separate declarations of that -- so the port a connection needed might not exist on the node. Which renderer shows is now read from what is wired: src/core.ts#shownMode. The same change map_output took at 0.15.0.

ontology.note: TableView activity is implemented; broader table artifact contracts remain open. `emits` records what the module named in implementation.definition asserts, and this widget is defined in src/core.ts#TYPES, which asserts nothing — the fw:TableView facts are built in the execution case and are gated by validate:ontology-coupling, which holds at zero undeclared. Same shape as map_output 0.15.0.

changes.description: Declare its own shape into the write-up. Every run now machines a note into the Results section of the Notes tab stating what this artifact is made of. Experiment 147 measured that a Results section is mostly artifacts rather than prose, and until now not one artifact in this application could put a single word into a write-up: the figure was drawn, the receipt recorded what it drew, and the Notes tab had nothing from it. THE NOTE CARRIES NO NUMBER, which is the rule the whole change is shaped around -- experiment 141's amendment of 2026-10-30 settled that a figure's number is computed when a document is rendered, from the note's position in the IMRaD outline and the venue's own convention, because setting one figure aside for a venue moves every number after it. A note that wrote "Table 1" into its text would be right when machined and wrong the first time somebody dragged a card. The note is editable like any machined note: editing it forks it into a note of the author's own and the machined one goes on being rewritten by every run. Only in the data-table mode: the point, polygon and decision modes are views of things that are not a published table. The note names the columns AS THE TABLE SPELLS THEM, in code spans, rather than forcing them into a sentence -- the first version wrote "${valueField} by ${keys}" and produced "per 1,000 people by group" on this application's own output, because `rateTable` sets the value field to a unit phrase and keys a long table by the literal word `measure`. A generator cannot know whether a column name is a noun, so it states them and leaves prose to the author. It also reports empty cells as unknown rather than zero, and names the source file and digest where the table came in as one. THE CAPTION IS NOT MACHINED AND IS NOT CLAIMED. The practitioner, 2026-10-30: "Captions are the user's responsibility, unless there is a way to machine it based on table, map, chart or equation semantics." Everything in this note is read off a declaration, which is the exception that rule names; the caption itself states the subject, the population, the place and the period in the author's words and none of that is derivable here. The first version of this release called its output a caption and filed it under a function word invented for the purpose, which claimed an authorial act while delivering something else -- the same error experiment 149 settled for notes in general, arriving one level down. What would make a real caption machinable is 147's chain for the machined title -- design, place, outcome, period -- of which only place is declared today.

evidence.note: Repository regression coverage exists; this release entry does not certify a widget independently. The self-description added in 0.6.0 is covered by tests/artifact-notes.test.mjs (13 unit checks, including that nothing machined numbers its own artifact or calls itself a caption, that an unnamed artifact is left unnamed rather than titled, and that a unit is stated once) and by tests/equation-notes.browser.mjs over the South London example on Chromium and WebKit. Both were mutation-checked by reintroducing the behaviour they forbid.
